newsitem.title: UK: Fewer small companies see UK economy improving - 3i.
newsitem.headline: Fewer small companies see UK economy improving - 3i.

text.p: Fewer small and medium-sized British companies reported an improvement in the business and economic climate in the first three months of the year, a survey from venture capital group 3i showed on Monday.
The survey also showed a fall in overall optimism of companies about their own prospects.
The 3i barometer index fell from 101 in November to 71 now, returning to its level in August last year. The index was based at 100 in January 1988.
Under 50 percent of companies surveyed expect profits to increase during this quarter, compared with more than 60 percent in November's survey.
But almost two-thirds expect to be employing more people by the end of the year than they were at the end of 1996.
"Compared with a year ago, the economic and business climate remains strongly positive," said 3i's chief executive, Ewen Macpherson.
"However, many small and medium-sized companies are exporters, or suppliers to exporters, and their less optimistic outlook may well reflect the impact of the appreciation of sterling on margins."
The pound has risen about 17 percent on a trade-weighted basis since last August.
The survey also asked whether firms' thought a single European currency would be good for business.
A positive balance of nine percent said it would help, down from 23 percent in May 1995.
The survey canvassed 1,000 companies in which 3i invests, of which 48.2 percent responded.
